title: Kids with smartphones have better mental health, study finds
content:

A big new long-term study from the University of South Florida has found that kids with smartphones report higher wellbeing than those without smartphones.

This is in line with an overwhelming amount of previous reporting on this issue, which shows that not only is there no actual link between smartphone use and poor mental health (despite what moral panic political actors like Jonathan Haidt like to claim), but smartphone use keeps kids connected and happy.

Of course, this study got almost zero media coverage because it doesn’t feed the debunked pseudoscience that people in power and groups like the Heritage Foundation are pushing related to smartphones and social media. As I’ve reported, the media and political class has spent much of the past few years pushing a complete moral panic about kids and tech, claiming nonsense like smartphones and social media are “poisoning kids minds” in order to pass censorship bills that restrict civil liberties online.

Pretty much every single top researcher who actually studies this topic has come out and said this is total BS. But their attempts to inject reason and factual information into these debates have been unsuccessful.

The irony is that the authors of this latest study admit that they wanted to find harm. Yet the data irrefutably debunked their preconceived notion that smartphones were harming children.

“We went into this study expecting to find what many researchers, teachers and other observers assume: smartphone ownership is harmful to children. Not only was that not the case, most of the time we found the opposite – that owning a smartphone was associated with positive outcomes,” said Justin D. Martin, lead researcher on the project and the Eleanor Poynter Jamison Chair in Media Ethics and Press Policy as USF.

The study was led by a team of researchers at the University of South Florida who surveyed more than 1,500 11-to-13-year-olds in the state. The findings will inform a 25-year national study that is tracking young people’s digital media use and wellbeing into adulthood.

I want to pull out some key findings, because I think they’re really important. The study found that:

  • Kids with smartphones report greater well-being than kids who don’t have smartphones.

  • Kids with smartphones are more likely to hang out with friends.

  • Kids with smartphones are more likely to exercise.

  • Kids with smartphones also more likely to feel good about themselves.

  • Kids with smartphones are more likely to seek help when they need it.

  • Kids with smartphones also less likely to use phrases such as “life often feels meaningless” or “I get very angry and often lose my temper.”

  • Kids with smartphones score better when it comes to self-esteem.

  • Kids with smartphones are less likely to be cyberbullied.

There are very clear reasons why reactionaries like Haidt and others are attempting to cut kids off from the internet. Lawmakers such as Marsha Blackburn, co-sponsor of the Kids Online Safety Act, a terrible censorship bill dressed up as “protecting kids” said that we need to restrict kids access from the internet and social media to protect them from the “transgender in society.”

Jonathan Haidt has promoted conspiracy theories about trans youth. I’m linking a good read on Haidt and the moral panic he’s profiting from below. Ezra Klein had Haidt on his podcast this week and allowed him to spew a whole bunch of nonsense unfortunately.

“A recent study of mental health outcomes and internet access in 202 countries — which is, yes, basically all of them — found no consistent correlations between screen time and negative mental effects. On top of that, suicide rates among teenagers are down despite going up for all other demographics, and longitudinal surveys show no decline in life satisfaction among teenagers since 2012. Which is a bit of a problem for Haidt’s thesis because social media and smartphones did not vanish by 2013,” journalist Greg Fish writes.

Based on their findings, the research team from University of South Florida, as well as a researcher from the Poynter Institute for Media Studies, provided a few recommendations for parents. The one negative effect smartphones were found to have on children was on sleep. Like a lot of us, kids will stay up too late using their smartphones in bed. Here are some of the experts’ recommendations:

  • Allowing children as young as 11 to have their own smartphone is likely fine and may be beneficial.

  • Don’t let kids sleep with their smartphones. One in four kids surveyed sleep with a smartphone in their hand or in bed. Children who keep their phones in their bed don’t get enough sleep compared to those who sleep with phones in another room (8.6 vs. 9.3 hours on average).

I’ll continue to cover this topic, but I hope this study can help counter the very well funded, extremely dangerous moral panic that is being pushed about kids and smartphones. Don’t fall for it!!
